title: Writing a clear email
examples: Should I use an email for my homework questions?
What is the difference between a formal and informal email?
How long should my email be?

explain.say: First you need a clear subject line for your email.
The subject line tells the reader what the email is about right away.

items: Help the reader know the topic

explain.say: Next you must use a polite greeting to start your message.
Your email should have one main purpose so the reader knows what to do.
After your message you need a polite closing to finish nicely.
For a real life example write to your teacher about a missed class.

items: Step 3: Body: I missed class today and need notes.

faq.q: How formal should my tone be in an email?
faq.a: You should keep your tone polite and respectful always. For a teacher, formal language is best.
asks: Is it okay to use slang?

faq.q: What if my email needs to cover two different topics?
faq.a: It is better to write two separate emails for two different topics. This keeps things clear.
asks: Should I write everything in one email?

faq.q: Do I need to use full sentences in my email?
faq.a: Yes you should use full sentences to make your message clear. Short notes can seem too casual.

faq.q: What is the difference between 'Thanks' and 'Sincerely'?
faq.a: Thanks is more casual for a quick reply. Sincerely is more formal for a main request.
asks: Which closing is better for a teacher?

faq.q: Does the subject line count towards my grade?
faq.a: No it does not count towards a grade but it helps the teacher read it quickly. A good subject line is very helpful.
asks: Does the teacher read the subject?

facts: A subject line summarizes the email content briefly.
Always start with a polite greeting like Dear [Name].
Every email should focus on one main purpose.
End with a polite closing such as Sincerely or Regards.

quiz.say: What should the subject line do?

options.show: B) Summarize the email's main topic
options.say: B) Summarize the email's main topic

options.show: C) Be very long and detailed
options.say: C) Be very long and detailed

quiz.why: The subject line must give the reader an instant idea of what the email is about.

wrong.0: Emojis are not appropriate for formal communication with a teacher.
wrong.2: This might confuse the reader and make them ignore the important message.
wrong.3: Long subjects are hard to read when looking at many emails.

quiz.say: If you are asking a question about homework, what is the best greeting?

options.show: C) To Whom It May Concern:
options.say: C) To Whom It May Concern:

quiz.why: A formal greeting shows respect for the person you are writing to.

wrong.0: This greeting is too casual for a teacher or school setting.
wrong.1: This is too general; you should address the person by name.
wrong.2: It is better to use a more complete and formal salutation.

quiz.say: If you write about homework, submitting a report, and asking for a meeting, what is the best practice?
quiz.show: A) Write it all in one big email.

options.show: B) Write separate emails for each topic.
options.say: B) Write separate emails for each topic.

options.show: A) Write it all in one big email.
options.say: A) Write it all in one big email.

options.show: C) Use bullet points for everything.
options.say: C) Use bullet points for everything.

options.show: D) Just write the main point quickly.
options.say: D) Just write the main point quickly.

quiz.why: Keeping topics separate makes it easier for the reader to understand and act on each point.

wrong.1: Mixing topics makes the email confusing and hard to follow.
wrong.2: While helpful, you still need clear paragraphs to explain the purpose.
wrong.3: You must still include a proper greeting and closing.
